text:
alex: CI deploy to prod started failing after we switched GH Actions to OIDC. getting a 403 from the token exchange step when trying to impersonate the ci-deployer service account.

alex: log snippet:
```
ERROR: 403 Permission 'iam.serviceAccounts.getAccessToken' denied for principal principalSet://iam.googleapis.com/projects/123/locations/global/workloadIdentityPools/github-pool/* on resource projects/123/serviceAccounts/ci-deployer@myproj.iam.gserviceaccount.com
{"error": "Request had insufficient authentication scopes"}
```

sana: hmm, that 403 usually means the provider principal in GCP doesn't match the token's audience/attributes. did you scope the workload identity pool to the repo? can you paste the SA IAM binding?

alex: here's what I see from `gcloud iam service-accounts get-iam-policy`:
```
resource: projects/123/serviceAccounts/ci-deployer@myproj.iam.gserviceaccount.com
bindings:
- role: roles/iam.serviceAccountTokenCreator
  members:
  - principalSet://iam.googleapis.com/projects/123/locations/global/workloadIdentityPools/github-pool/*
```

sana: that principalSet is very broad. we usually grant a more specific principal like `principal://iam.googleapis.com/projects/123/locations/global/workloadIdentityPools/github-pool/attribute.repository/our-org/our-repo`. also verify the GH Action requests an id-token with the correct audience (`id-token: write`).

alex: workflow snippet for auth looks like this:
```
- name: Authenticate to GCP
  uses: google-github-actions/auth@v0
  with:
    workload_identity_provider: 'projects/123/locations/global/workloadIdentityPools/github-pool/providers/github'
    service_account: 'ci-deployer@myproj.iam.gserviceaccount.com'
```

maria: quick repro steps: locally run `gcloud auth print-identity-token --audiences=https://github.com/our-org/our-repo` and then pass it to your token-exchange endpoint to see if GCP accepts it. also decode the token (jwt.io) to check `aud` and `exp`. GH id-tokens are short-lived — GH often issues ~60s tokens; if your token exchange expects longer TTL you might hit a timing/expiry problem.

jara: also make sure the provider condition (if used) matches `attribute.repository` exactly. a common gotcha: provider condition left to `our-org/old-repo` after repo rename.

alex: I updated the workflow to log the raw id-token and decoded values; here's the decoded payload we printed:
```
{
  "aud": "https://github.com/our-org/our-repo",
  "iss": "https://token.actions.githubusercontent.com",
  "exp": 1700000000,
  "sub": "repo:our-org/our-repo:ref:refs/heads/main"
}
```

sana: thanks — aud looks right. exp looks suspicious (that's older than expected in my env). can you confirm the GH runner clock and that tokens aren't being cached between steps? also confirm the `audience` configured on the Workload Identity provider (in GCP console) accepts that exact string.

alex: double-checked runner clocks — all good. i ran `gcloud auth print-identity-token --audiences=https://github.com/our-org/our-repo` locally and the identity token we generated worked against the GCP token exchange endpoint. but in Actions the token seems to fail.

maria: when GHA requests id-token, it uses `actions/checkout` and `id-token: write`. confirm your job has `permissions: id-token: write` at the workflow level. if it does, the next suspect is the pool provider mapping: maybe it includes an attribute condition tied to `repository` that still points to `old-repo`.

alex: i checked the provider config in GCP — indeed the provider's attribute condition had `attribute.repository == "our-org/old-repo"`. i updated it to `our-org/our-repo` and re-ran the workflow. initial deploys started succeeding. :tada:

jara: great find. ops-bot: create follow-up ticket to add repo check to onboarding checklist.

ops-bot: [audit] Created ticket SUP-9876 - "Workload Identity provider repository mismatch causing CI 403" assigned to sana.

sana: writeup / remediation steps we did: 1) decode failing id-token to confirm aud and sub; 2) verify GH Actions job has `permissions: id-token: write`; 3) inspect workload identity provider attribute conditions for `attribute.repository`; 4) ensure SA binding uses either a precise `principal://.../attribute.repository/our-org/our-repo` or an appropriate principalSet with a condition; 5) avoid increasing token_lifetime_seconds on impersonation calls — rely on default short TTLs, or ensure client's clock and caching are correct.

maria: please add a short runbook for teams migrating to OIDC: checklist should include provider audience, repository condition, `id-token: write`, SA roles (roles/iam.serviceAccountTokenCreator or roles/iam.serviceAccountUser as needed), and how to decode/inspect id-tokens.

jara: added a draft runbook PR (#42) with the checklist and a minimal repro.

sana: i'll close SUP-9876 after PR merges and we verify no other repos are mis-configured.

alex: thanks everyone — deploying again looks green. will follow up if anything else pops up.
